speaker: Doctor
text:
Can you describe exactly how the bleeding started, and have you noticed any bruising on your arms or legs recently?

Also, tell me if you or your family have ever had problems with blood clotting or if any previous lab tests have been abnormal.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with platelet count and bleeding time.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT (CBC) WITH PLATELET COUNT: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal); BLEEDING TIME: Not explicitly provided in the source data (though clinical findings of petechiae and gum bleeding suggest a functional platelet defect despite normal count).

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I see; have you noticed any prolonged bleeding after minor cuts or gums bleeding while brushing your teeth? Additionally, do you have any joint pain, swelling, or unexplained bone pain?

REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile (PT/INR, PTT) and Platelet Function Assay.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photo of petechiae and ecchymosis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal); Special Test: ELISA Binding Assay findings indicate Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.
